notes: Paging: variables are read with per_page=30 and secrets with per_page=100, one page each. With 31 variables the 31st shows 'not set' though it is set; with 101 secrets the 101st shows 'not set'. The spec puts no limit on how many there are.

After a request body over 10 000 characters the board answers without reading the rest, and the next request on the same kept-alive connection sometimes fails: ECONNRESET after a 1 MB body, or a spurious 'That request didn't make sense.' for a valid 4 000-character save after several big ones. readJson is unchanged from the base, but the Settings box is the first place a person can paste that much. ac6_problems.mjs sends big bodies on their own connections.
Error answers are two short sentences (for example 'The box is empty. Paste the value first.'). Counted as plain, as #10's checks did for the same words.
Values are trimmed: '  key-with-spaces\n' is saved as 'key-with-spaces'. A value of only spaces is 'The box is empty.' The spec says nothing about it.
A set checks setting says 'Ella set this for the team's checks.'; an unset one says 'Ella fills this in for the team's checks. Ask her in your chat.'
The Settings page's footer says 'It changes your project only when you press Save here.'; the board's says '... only when you save a setting.'
Make on an entry without make: random is refused ('The board can't make this one up. Paste the real value.'), with nothing sent.
A list file that isn't JSON gives no items and skipped 1 (the page says some of the list didn't make sense); a file with no settings array gives 'Nothing to set yet.'
A GitHub 5xx on save comes back to the page as HTTP 400 (dropped connection: 502). Only the sentence reaches the person.
